analysis.investment_thesis: Anant Raj is a classic turnaround/cyclical — revenue collapsed from INR 431 Cr (2016) to INR 250 Cr (2021) and has since surged to INR 2,060 Cr (2025), with a new data center business adding a genuine growth kicker. Forward PEG is attractive (~0.7x on 22x forward P/E), but sub-12% ROE and lumpy real estate OCF keep me cautious.
key_strengths: Dramatic debt reduction: borrowings fell from INR 1,691 Cr (2020) to INR 563 Cr (2025) while equity nearly doubled — a de-leveraging turnaround I can respect
Data center segment adds a high-multiple, recurring-revenue overlay to a traditionally cyclical real estate base — optionality the market may not fully price
Revenue CAGR of 19% over 9 years with net profit at 22% CAGR, and recent trajectory (9 Cr→426 Cr profit in four years) is genuinely impressive
key_risks: ROE of 10.9% and ROCE of 11.2% are both below my 12% minimum — the business isn't yet earning attractive returns on its large asset base (INR 5,446 Cr)
Real estate operating cash flow is volatile (3/5 positive OCF years) — the sector is inherently lumpy and dependent on project completion timing
The stock has re-rated sharply on data center hype; if execution disappoints or macro slows, the P/E of 35x is hard to defend for a real estate developer
red_flags: OCF was negative in FY24 (INR -26 Cr) despite strong reported profits — working capital absorption in real estate can mask earnings quality
The nine-year history includes a brutal earnings collapse (profit fell from INR 76 Cr to INR 9 Cr); management's track record through cycles is mixed
Balance sheet still carries INR 563 Cr in borrowings against a data center build-out; capex is rising (INR 77 Cr in FY25) and FCF remains thin (INR 20 Cr)
analysis.detailed_analysis: I classify Anant Raj as a turnaround with a fast-grower overlay — a combination that can be very rewarding if the data center story delivers. The NCR real estate recovery is visible and real, and the pivot to data centers is smart positioning for India's AI/cloud infrastructure wave. The balance sheet cleanup is commendable — D/E down to 0.13 from 0.68 in 2020. On forward numbers (P/E 22x vs expected 30-35% growth), the PEG of ~0.65-0.70 is genuinely attractive by my standards. However, ROE below 12% means the company isn't yet generating superior returns on capital, and real estate cyclicality means I need to see two or three more consistent quarters before I'd call this a conviction buy. Hold for now; buy on confirmation of data center revenue contribution and ROE crossing 14%.
